basis: Benign ovarian neoplasm; reproductive organs have no axis.
HADH-related hyperinsulinism; supplied HPO reports steatosis with elevated transaminases and hypoglycemic encephalopathy in 80-99%. Retinopathy and neuropathy are below 30%.
Leukoencephalopathy with developmental delay, spasticity and dysarthria. Urinary urgency alone does not establish urinary tract damage.
Brachydactyly and hypertension define the syndrome. Stroke is a separately diagnosed complication of hypertension.
Lysosomal storage with skeletal disease and developmental impairment; valve dysfunction 80-99%. Skin and gingival disease 80-99%, hearing and airway dysfunction 30-79% omitted by cap.
Metaplastic alteration of gastric mucosa; subsequent cancer risk does not add another axis.
Localized benign hepatic mass with fibrohistiocytic inflammation; an autoimmune or other specific immune-mediated mechanism is not established.
Immune-mediated juvenile polyarthritis. Uveitis is below 30% in ANA-negative polyarticular disease.
Cerebellar malformation and developmental impairment; skeletal dysplasia and chorioretinal coloboma each 2/2, atrioventricular canal defect 1/2. Frequencies derive from very small samples.
Inherited isolated nail disorder with onycholysis.
Benign neoplasm of breast parenchyma; breast has no axis.
Inherited hypertrophic narrowing of the gastric pylorus.
Chronic airway disease driven by type 2 immune inflammation.
Hereditary toe malformation with an annotated skeletal abnormality.
Neurodevelopmental disease; pes planus 2/2 with additional skeletal defects, strabismus 2/2. Isolated tricuspid regurgitation has uncertain significance; hepatomegaly alone is insufficient.
Degeneration of autonomic nerves. Hypotension, sweating changes, bowel and bladder symptoms reflect denervation without established direct damage to those organs.
Combined pituitary hormone deficiency; supplied phenotypes do not establish additional organ damage.
Mosaic NF2 causes nerve-sheath tumors; vestibular involvement with hearing impairment is common (>30%). Ocular and skin involvement varies with mosaic distribution.
Congenital ocular motor nerve dysinnervation causes restricted eye movement and globe retraction. Hearing impairment 3/14 (~21%) is below threshold.
Umbrella for diseases of the uvea; an infectious or immune mechanism does not apply across the entire group.
Chromaffin neuroendocrine tumor of sympathetic paraganglia or adrenal medulla. Catecholamine-related hypertension does not establish direct cardiovascular damage.
Pregnancy-associated hypertension with proteinuria defines vascular and renal involvement. Neurologic injury occurs in the eclampsia subset.
Ichthyosis with hair abnormalities; corneal opacity 1/3 (~33%) supports ocular damage. Photophobia alone is insufficient; conical incisors lack documented functional damage.
Familial erythrocytosis with increased red-cell mass, hemoglobin and hematocrit.
Umbrella for diseases anatomically involving the ear; infection is only one subset.
